translation_notes: prefixes: RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, SH->sh, XSD->xsd (RDF and RDFS stay unused, as in original.py: kept only because the source file imports them).

the two reads are `next(self.sh.shaclg.objects(s, SH.property))`, matched by strata trav_one_step/trav_single_value at once: each becomes `m{ {s} sh:property ?prop }(self.sh.shaclg).first()`. `self.sh.shaclg` is not the file's single current graph (it is reassigned mid-function, `self.sh.shaclg = Graph()`, twice) so the call suffix `(self.sh.shaclg)` supplies it explicitly rather than `@graph`.

`.first()` differs from `next()` on the empty case (None vs StopIteration) -- the canonical rewrite in how-to/migrate-from-rdflib.md accepts this; here it is moot, since get_ngsild_property_constraints (context_shim.py) always leaves shapes[0]/s with exactly one sh:property triple for the value_rank/datatype combinations this test drives.

left untranslated on purpose: `(inner, SH.path, ...) in list(self.sh.shaclg)` uses `list(g)`, an unfiltered full-graph scan explicitly kept as `list(g)` by querying.md (#keep-listg-for-a-full-scan); the second `(inner, SH.path, ...) in self.sh.shaclg` is plain Graph.__contains__, not part of the strata this region was drawn for (trav_existence is a different stratum) and not degrading anything m{ } would express here, so left as ordinary rdflib.

context_shim.py restores `Shacl` (lib/shacl.py) trimmed to exactly the methods this region's two calls reach -- the pipeline's context window captures the test method body but not sibling classes the test file imports. driver.py restores the missing `TestShaclAdditional.setUp()` fixture as a small stand-in with its own __eq__ (RDF isomorphism on .sh.shaclg/.data_graph), needed because the region mutates its `self` argument so the two sides cannot share one instance to sidestep object comparison, unlike the swrl2rdf trav_single_value precedent.

Correction du 2026-10-31 (audit par mutation) : les deux `next(self.sh.shaclg.objects(s, SH.property))` traduits par `.first()` n'étaient pas fidèles. Sur une bibliothèque régressée (forme sans sh:property), l'original lève StopIteration ; `.first()` rendait None, et `(None, sh:path, hasValueList) in self.sh.shaclg` est un joker : le test passait en silence sur une bibliothèque cassée. Preuve : appels no_list_property et no_scalar_property du pilote renforcé, FAIL avec `.first()`. Corrigé en `next(iter(m{ … }(self.sh.shaclg)))`, la seule forme fidèle à un `next()` sans défaut ; `.first()` retiré de `constructions`. La note précédente qui jugeait l'écart « moot » ne valait que pour la bibliothèque intacte.

repair.driver: renforcé : journal des assert* (méthode, membres à nœuds anonymes masqués, issue) comparé par __eq__, messages d'échec masqués de même ; quatre appels contre une bibliothèque régressée, sous-classes de Shacl identiques des deux côtés : forme de liste sans sh:property, forme scalaire sans sh:property, sh:path hasValue au lieu de hasValueList, sh:property d'un nœud auxiliaire émis avant celui de la forme.
